card.name: Word 'to' after dose reduction
card.fires_on: The word 'to' (sometimes 'that') right after a verb phrase about reducing or adjusting a drug's dose, just before the new target amount. Seen in interaction and dose-adjustment instructions.

modes.label: The phrase 'reduce dose to'
modes.description: 'to' after 'decrease/reduce/adjust the dose of [drug]', where a new dose figure comes next.
modes.example: Avoid use with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors; if unavoidable, decrease the dosage of MOVANTIK<< to>> 12.5 mg once daily

modes.label: Same-amount 'that'
modes.description: 'that' after 'the dosage of [drug]' in conversion instructions, introducing the matching amount.
modes.example: Patients should receive the dosage of glycerol phenylbutyrate oral liquid<< that>> contains the same amount of phenylbut

card.writes: It seems to prepare the model for a computed or matched amount, such as an estimate or ratio.
card.plain: It responds to the word 'to' (sometimes 'that') in a dose-change instruction, at the point where the new dose is about to be named.
evidence: Decrease guanfacine extended-release tablets<< to>> 50% of target dosage when
reduce the dose of KISQAL<<I>> to 200 mg once daily
Reduce tolterodine tartrate extended-release capsules dose<< to>> 2 mg once daily.

wording_before.name: Word 'to' after dose reduction
wording_before.plain: It fires at the point in a dose-change instruction where the new dose is about to be named.
